title: Azure AI Fundamentals
subtitle: Climb the money ladder — one AI question per grade level

gradeLabels.f: F-RANK -- Back to the Training Data

options: A computer that can only do math calculations
Software that enables machines to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence
A robot that can walk and talk like a person
A database that stores large amounts of information
questions.note: AI enables machines to simulate human intelligence — things like recognizing speech, understanding language, and making decisions. It is not limited to math or physical robots.

explain.correct: AI is software that lets machines do things requiring human intelligence, such as understanding images, translating language, and making predictions.
wrong: Calculators perform math but have no intelligence — they cannot learn, reason, or recognize patterns.
Physical robots are one application of AI, but AI itself is software — not a mechanical body.
Databases store data but cannot learn, reason, or make decisions on their own.

questions.q: An app reads a photo and identifies whether it shows a cat or a dog. Which AI workload does this describe?
questions.note: Computer Vision is the AI workload that deals with images and video. NLP works with text and spoken language, while Anomaly Detection finds outliers in data.

explain.correct: Computer Vision enables machines to interpret and understand images — identifying objects, classifying photos, and detecting faces.
wrong: NLP (Natural Language Processing) handles text and spoken language, not images.
Anomaly Detection identifies unusual data points — for example, a fraudulent bank transaction — not image content.
Generative AI creates new content such as text, images, or code — it does not classify existing photos.

questions.q: A model is trained on a dataset where each house has a price tag already attached. What type of machine learning is this?
questions.note: Supervised learning uses labeled training data — each example has a known correct answer (the label). Unsupervised learning has no labels and finds patterns on its own.

explain.correct: Supervised learning trains on labeled examples. Here, each house (feature set) comes with a known price (label), so the model learns the relationship between features and price.
wrong: Unsupervised learning has no labels — the algorithm discovers hidden patterns or groups without being told the correct answer.
Reinforcement learning trains an agent through trial-and-error and reward signals, not pre-labeled datasets.
Deep learning is an architecture (neural networks with many layers) — it can be supervised or unsupervised, so deep learning alone does not answer the question.

questions.q: A supervised ML model predicts next month's electricity usage in kilowatt-hours for a building. What type of ML problem is this?
questions.note: Regression predicts a continuous numeric value. Classification predicts a discrete category (e.g., spam vs. not spam). Kilowatt-hours is a number, so this is regression.

explain.correct: Regression outputs a continuous number — kilowatt-hours is a numeric quantity, making this a regression problem.
wrong: Classification predicts a discrete category or class label (e.g., 'high usage' vs 'low usage'), not a raw numeric value.
Clustering is unsupervised — it groups similar data points without predicting a specific output value.
Anomaly detection identifies unusual or unexpected data points; it does not predict a future numeric value.

questions.q: A loan approval model consistently approves applications from one demographic group at a higher rate than equally qualified applicants from another group. Which Microsoft Responsible AI principle is being violated?
questions.note: Fairness means AI systems should treat all people equitably and avoid reinforcing historical biases. Differential outcomes for equally qualified groups is a fairness failure.

explain.correct: Fairness requires that AI systems treat all people equitably regardless of race, gender, or other characteristics. Differential approval rates for equally qualified applicants is a classic bias/fairness violation.
wrong: Reliability and Safety means the system behaves as expected and does not cause unintended harm — it addresses errors and safe operation, not demographic bias.
Transparency means people can understand how the AI makes decisions — related to explainability, not demographic outcome disparities.

Inclusiveness means AI should benefit and empower all people, including those with disabilities — it overlaps with fairness but focuses on access and participation, not on equal treatment of equally qualified individuals.

questions.q: A vision system draws a bounding box around every car and pedestrian in a traffic camera image, labeling each box with the object type. Which computer vision task is this?
questions.note: Object detection locates objects in an image and draws bounding boxes around them, providing both a class label and a position. Image classification assigns one label to the whole image without locating individual objects.

explain.correct: Object detection identifies WHERE objects are (bounding box coordinates) and WHAT they are (class label) — exactly what the traffic-camera system does for cars and pedestrians.
wrong: Image classification assigns a single label to the whole image (e.g., 'traffic scene') — it does not locate or draw boxes around individual objects.
OCR extracts text from images — it does not detect or classify physical objects like cars and pedestrians.
Semantic segmentation classifies every pixel of an image into a category, producing a colored mask rather than bounding boxes.

questions.q: A customer support pipeline extracts the names of products and companies mentioned in support tickets. Which NLP technique does this use?
questions.note: NER identifies and classifies named entities — people, organizations, locations, products — within text. Sentiment analysis determines positive or negative tone; key phrase extraction pulls out important terms, not entity types.

explain.correct: Named Entity Recognition (NER) scans text and tags spans as specific entity types such as Product, Organization, or Location — exactly what is needed to extract product and company names.
wrong: Sentiment analysis determines the emotional tone of text (positive, negative, neutral) — it does not identify specific named entities.
Language detection identifies which language a piece of text is written in — it does not extract entity names.
Key phrase extraction pulls out the most important words or phrases in text, but does not classify them into entity types like Product or Organization.

questions.q: A developer needs to transcribe recorded customer call audio into text and then detect the language of the transcript. Which TWO Azure AI services are best suited for these tasks respectively?
options: Azure AI Vision and Azure AI Language
Azure AI Speech and Azure AI Language
Azure OpenAI Service and Azure AI Vision
Azure AI Translator and Azure AI Speech
questions.note: Azure AI Speech handles audio-to-text transcription (speech-to-text). Azure AI Language handles text-based NLP tasks including language detection, sentiment, and NER.

explain.correct: Azure AI Speech provides speech-to-text transcription for audio. Azure AI Language provides NLP capabilities including language detection — the correct pair for these two tasks.
wrong: Azure AI Vision analyzes images and video, not audio. Pairing it with Azure AI Language handles language detection correctly but uses the wrong service for audio transcription.
Azure OpenAI Service provides generative AI (GPT/DALL-E) and does not perform direct audio-to-text transcription. Azure AI Vision works with images, not audio.

Azure AI Translator translates text between languages but is not a transcription service. While Azure AI Speech is correct for transcription, Translator does not perform language detection as a primary NLP service.

questions.q: A cancer-screening model flags 90 actual cancer cases as positive and misses 10 real cancer cases. It also raises 20 false alarms on healthy patients. What is the model's recall?
questions.note: Recall = TP / (TP + FN). There are 90 true positives and 10 false negatives (missed cancers), so recall = 90 / (90 + 10) = 90%. The 20 false positives affect precision, not recall.

explain.correct: Recall = TP / (TP + FN) = 90 / (90 + 10) = 90/100 = 90%. Recall measures the model's ability to find all actual positive cases; false positives do not factor into recall.
wrong: 82% would be 90/110 — this incorrectly includes the 20 false positives (FP) in the denominator. FP belongs in the precision formula, not recall.
75% would be 90/120 — this also incorrectly adds false positives to the denominator, confusing precision and recall.
69% would be 90/130 — this adds both FP and FN to the denominator, which matches no standard metric formula.

questions.q: An Azure OpenAI-powered chatbot confidently states an incorrect historical date that sounds plausible but was never in its training data or context window. What term describes this failure, and which technique most directly reduces it?
options: Overfitting — prevented by training on more data
Hallucination — reduced by grounding the model with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
Underfitting — prevented by using a larger language model
Bias — reduced by using reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)
questions.note: Hallucination occurs when an LLM generates plausible-sounding but factually incorrect content. RAG (grounding) retrieves verified documents and injects them into the prompt context, anchoring the model's response to real sources.

explain.correct: Hallucination is when an LLM produces confident but false information. RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) grounds responses by fetching relevant verified documents and including them in the prompt, reducing hallucination.
wrong: Overfitting means a model memorizes training data and generalizes poorly to new data — it is not the term for generating false information, and adding more training data does not anchor outputs to verified facts.
Underfitting means a model is too simple to capture patterns, producing poor predictions — it does not describe confident fabrication of false facts.

Bias refers to systematic unfairness in model outputs (e.g., demographic disparities). RLHF can improve alignment but does not specifically anchor model outputs to verified factual sources the way RAG does.

questions.q: Which statement about transformer-based LLM tokenization is precisely correct as it applies to Azure OpenAI billing and model behavior?
options: Each token corresponds to exactly one word; a 1,000-word document uses exactly 1,000 tokens
Tokens are full sentences; longer sentences cost more because each sentence is one token
A token is roughly 0.75 words on average in English; billing is per token for both prompt and completion, and common words may be a single token while rare words may be split into multiple tokens
Tokenization converts text into floating-point embedding vectors; each vector is one token and costs one billing unit
questions.note: Azure OpenAI bills per token for input (prompt) and output (completion). A token averages ~0.75 English words (~4 characters). Common words are usually one token; uncommon or technical words may split into subword tokens.

explain.correct: A token averages ~0.75 English words (~4 characters). Billing counts tokens for both the prompt and the completion. Common words are often one token; rare or long words split into subword pieces — this is why token count does not equal word count.
wrong: Tokens do not equal words one-for-one. A word like 'tokenization' may be split into multiple tokens ('token', 'ization'), and punctuation and spaces also consume tokens. A 1,000-word document typically uses roughly 1,300 tokens.
Tokens are subword units, not sentences. Splitting at sentence boundaries would make context windows far too small and does not reflect how transformers work.
Embeddings are floating-point vector representations of tokens used internally by the transformer — they are not the same as tokens. An embedding is derived from a token; it is not a billing unit.
